title: Drishyam 3 Crosses Rs 501.80 Crore Worldwide as Day 12 Collections Rebound
excerpt: Ajay Devgn's thriller recovered on its second Tuesday after a Monday fall, with Sacnilk putting Day 12 India net at Rs 8.50 crore and the worldwide gross past Rs 500 crore.
body:
• Drishyam 3: The Conclusion crossed Rs 501.80 crore in worldwide gross in 12 days, according to Sacnilk figures reported on October 13.
  • Sacnilk put Day 12 India net at Rs 8.50 crore from 14,846 shows, up 41.7% from Monday's Rs 6.00 crore, taking India net to Rs 323.50 crore.
  • Trackers differ by metric: one India gross tracker put Day 12 at Rs 9.06 crore and the India gross total at Rs 393.23 crore, so net and gross figures should not be mixed.
  • Director Abhishek Pathak has ruled out a fourth Hindi film, calling this instalment the conclusion of Vijay Salgaonkar's story.

Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3: The Conclusion recovered on its second Tuesday after a sharp second-Monday fall, crossing Rs 500 crore worldwide on Day 12. According to Sacnilk, the film collected Rs 8.50 crore net in India on Tuesday, October 13, across 14,846 shows. That was a 41.7% rise from the Rs 6.00 crore net reported for Monday.

The Day 12 result took the film's India net total to Rs 323.50 crore and its India gross to Rs 387.80 crore, Sacnilk said. Overseas, it added Rs 2.50 crore on Day 12, taking the overseas gross to Rs 114.00 crore and the worldwide gross to Rs 501.80 crore.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=BSZZwBaNQAA

Why the percentages differ

Readers will see different jump figures in different reports, and the gap is about what is being measured. Sacnilk's 41.7% is a net-to-net comparison for India. A separate tracked-gross table from Track Tollywood put Day 12 India gross at Rs 9.06 crore, up 27.5% from its Day 11 gross figure of Rs 7.10 crore, with a tracked India gross total of Rs 393.23 crore. India Today's headline report described an 18% jump after the second-Monday slump. The underlying direction is consistent across trackers - Tuesday rose after Monday's drop - but the exact percentage depends on whether a tracker is using net or gross, and on its own show-level estimates. None of these figures is a producer-confirmed total.

https://x.com/Trendswoodcom/status/2109694782113186102

The pattern behind the bounce is clearer than any single percentage. The film opened on October 2, and Sacnilk's summary puts Week 1 India net at Rs 245.50 crore. The second weekend held up before Monday's fall to Rs 6.00 crore net, the kind of weekday drop a film in its second week normally faces once the opening audience has been exhausted. Tuesday's recovery, with 607,519 footfalls on Day 12 and cumulative footfalls of 13,630,503 in Sacnilk's count, suggests word of mouth is still bringing in viewers rather than the run relying only on opening-week demand.

Occupancy on Day 12

Sacnilk reported Hindi 2D occupancy strongest at night. In its regional table, Pune recorded 26.3% overall occupancy, Mumbai 24.8%, Bengaluru 24.5% and the National Capital Region 22.5%, while Hyderabad and Surat were each at 9.5%. The spread matters for the film's next week: metros are still filling evening and night shows, which is where a thriller with a familiar lead tends to sustain its run, while weaker daytime occupancy in some centres leaves it exposed if screens are cut for new releases.

"It has to actually take the characters somewhere and give the audience a feeling that this journey has reached its final point."

- Abhishek Pathak, Director

No fourth Hindi film, the director says

The box office run is playing out against a firm creative endpoint. Director Abhishek Pathak has ruled out a fourth Hindi instalment, a position reported by Variety India and in an interview with Bollywood Hungama, where he said the film is called The Conclusion because it had to bring the characters' journey to a final point and end on a good note. Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar, with Tabu, Shriya Saran and Rajat Kapoor reprising their roles and Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj joining the cast, according to Variety India.

For diaspora viewers who have followed the Hindi films alongside the Malayalam originals, this is the end of the Hindi Salgaonkar arc regardless of what happens in other versions.

What to watch next

The test now is the third weekend. If the film holds a meaningful share of its second-week screens, the Rs 501.80 crore worldwide gross reported at Day 12 will keep climbing on metro evening shows and overseas collections, which already account for Rs 114.00 crore of the total. If weekday occupancy slides back toward Monday's level, exhibitors will trim shows quickly. Either way, readers should treat daily tracker numbers as estimates that can be revised, and compare like with like - net with net, gross with gross - before drawing conclusions about the size of any one day's jump.
